solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Could it be five gold rings one’s received? (7)

indicatorNotes.rings: to ring something is to encircle it, so V and OR go round the rest

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether a present of five gold rings, as in the carol, has turned up.
annotation.walkthrough: The carol's 'five gold rings' is split three ways: V, OR, and 'rings' as the instruction to go round IS IT. A visitor is literally someone received.
annotation.definitionFit: A visitor is a person who is received by a host.

entries.clue: Long hollow source of Venetian marble (6)

indicatorNotes.source of: a source is where something starts, so take the first letter

blocks.note: an alley is a large playing marble

annotation.surface: A description of a long hollow space where Venetian marble is quarried.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants marble as stone for Venetian palaces; it is the children's toy, and an alley is a kind of marble.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a long depression running between hills is what geographers call a valley.

entries.clue: Hail is misconstrued, undone by Welsh language (7)

indicatorNotes.misconstrued: read wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order
indicatorNotes.undone: taken apart, so the letters are rearranged along with the W

annotation.surface: Someone's greeting is misunderstood and their Welsh lets them down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Welsh language' looks like the definition phrase; only 'language' is, and Welsh supplies a single W to the jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu language widely spoken in East Africa.

entries.clue: However elected, the new Turkish leader comes first (4,5)

indicatorNotes.comes first: tells you to put THE N AGA before IN

blocks.note: an aga was an Ottoman commander or chief
a candidate who is elected is in

annotation.surface: A political report: whoever wins the vote, the new Turkish leader takes precedence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turkish leader' suggests a first letter, T; here it is an Ottoman title. The clue reads back to front: 'comes first' puts the new leader ahead of the elected.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Then again' introduces a contrary point, just as 'however' does.

entries.clue: Taking back couple crying about missing lad’s debut (11)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.missing: lacking, so the L is removed
indicatorNotes.debut: a first appearance, so the first letter of lad

blocks.note: first letter of lad, the letter that goes

annotation.surface: A couple, tearful, taking their boy back after he failed to make his first appearance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Couple' and 'crying' are used as printed letters, not for their meanings; take the L out and jumble what is left.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the military sense: an army moving back into land it lost is recapturing it.

entries.clue: Stretching out, snake biting back of heel (7)

indicatorNotes.back of: the back of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
a biting wind is a raw wind

annotation.surface: A snake bites someone's heel as they lie sprawled out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Biting' is a verb on the surface, with the snake doing the biting; it is an adjective, as in biting cold, and means RAW.
annotation.definitionFit: Asprawl means sprawling, stretched out.

entries.clue: Put together some speed dating tips (3)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters are used
indicatorNotes.tips: tips over, so the letters run backwards, upwards in a down clue

annotation.surface: Advice for combining a few hints on speed dating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tips' reads as advice; it is the instruction to tip the hidden letters over.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: combining things, or summing numbers, is the basic sense of the verb.

entries.clue: What starts producing rainbows if suitably manipulated? (5)

annotation.definition: What starts producing rainbows if suitably manipulated?

indicatorNotes.What starts: take what starts each following word, their first letters

annotation.surface: A riddle about what makes rainbows when handled correctly.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the first letters spell PRISM, and a prism turned to the light does produce rainbows.
annotation.definitionFit: A prism, turned the right way in light, splits it into a rainbow.

entries.clue: Betting site, a popular source of windfall (7)

blocks.note: windfalls are fruit blown down from a tree

annotation.surface: A gambling venue described as a popular place to win big.
annotation.walkthrough: A windfall is money out of the blue on the surface and fallen fruit underneath. AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse where the Grand National horse race is run.
annotation.definitionFit: Aintree is a racecourse, so a place where bets are placed.

entries.clue: Turner possibly behind houses in classical style (8)

indicatorNotes.houses: to house something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: Tina Turner, the singer; 'possibly' flags an example

annotation.surface: A note that a painter such as Turner was working behind the classical style of his time.
annotation.walkthrough: Turner the capitalised name suggests the painter J M W Turner; it is Tina Turner the singer.
annotation.definitionFit: Latinate describes style derived from Latin, the classical language.

entries.clue: Left husband living in moderate, unfashionable property (9)

indicatorNotes.living in: to live in is to be inside, so H goes into the next pieces

blocks.note: to ease off is to moderate

annotation.surface: A woman leaves her husband, who lives in a modest, dated house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' reads as an adjective for a house; it is the verb, as in easing off. The husband sits in the join between the last two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a flat or house held for a fixed term from a freeholder is one kind of property.

entries.clue: Nothing odd in winning appeal, wouldn’t you agree? (5)

indicatorNotes.Nothing odd in: none of the odd letters in the next word are kept, only the even ones

annotation.surface: Someone argues that there is nothing strange in a successful appeal, and wants agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nothing odd' reads as 'nothing strange'; it is an instruction to throw away the odd letters.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Innit' is slang for 'isn't it', a tag asking for agreement.

entries.clue: Show technology advanced by Tesla? (5)

blocks.note: a Tesla is an example of an EV, an electric vehicle
A = advanced, as in A level

annotation.surface: A question about whether a technology demonstration was pushed forward by Tesla.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Show' is a musical, not a demonstration. 'Advanced by' puts EV ahead of IT A.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical about Eva Perón is one West End show.

entries.clue: American river choked by container vessel (9)

indicatorNotes.choked by: gripped round the throat, so held inside

blocks.note: the Tamar runs between Devon and Cornwall

annotation.surface: An American river clogged up by a shipping container.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Container vessel' reads as one thing, a container ship; the words split, with the can round the river and 'vessel' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled boat, a vessel.

entries.clue: Peril dissipated, councillor enters town sporting honour (6,5)

indicatorNotes.dissipated: scattered, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.enters: goes inside, so the pieces are put into TOWN

blocks.note: used as printed, and RIPLE CR goes in after the T

annotation.surface: A councillor brushes off danger and walks into a town wearing a medal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' looks like 'wearing'; it belongs with 'honour' as the definition. Cr for councillor is the British abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A Triple Crown is a sporting honour, for example in rugby or horse racing.

entries.clue: Before program preparation, briefly record frustration (14)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.Before: tells you DIS comes before APP OINTMENT

blocks.note: DISC with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: Someone vents frustration at having to note it all down before getting a computer program ready.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Preparation' reads as getting ready; it is a medical preparation, a cream or ointment.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the feeling when hopes are thwarted is frustration.

entries.clue: Most problematic in trial, fruitcake is regularly unavailable (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the next piece goes inside TEST
indicatorNotes.regularly unavailable: every other letter is not there

blocks.note: the even letters of fRuItCaKe Is

annotation.surface: A court trial made harder because an eccentric is often absent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' in the surface is a slang word for an odd person; here it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both superlatives: tricky means awkward or problematic, and -est makes it the most so.

entries.clue: Waste initially cleared after a flush (8)

indicatorNotes.initially cleared: the first letter is cleared away
indicatorNotes.after: tells you the piece comes after A

annotation.surface: A lavatory: waste goes once the toilet is flushed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flush' is the toilet on the surface and the adjective underneath: flush with cash.
annotation.definitionFit: Flush and affluent both mean having plenty of money.

entries.clue: Journal lacking nothing in review of semi-final action (9,5)

indicatorNotes.lacking: without, so the O is removed
indicatorNotes.in review of: looked over again, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: nothing = O, the letter that goes

annotation.surface: A newspaper runs a report on a semi-final, with nothing left out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a sports page; the definition is the Financial Times, a London daily newspaper, so the journal itself is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The Financial Times is a newspaper, and a daily paper is a journal.

entries.clue: Amphibians putting away jack rabbits (7)

indicatorNotes.putting away: putting something away removes it, here JACK

annotation.surface: Toads eating a jackrabbit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jack rabbits' reads as one animal; 'rabbits' is the verb for chattering on, and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is to natter, chat at length.

entries.clue: Customer ultimately tolerates having residence knocked about (3,4)

indicatorNotes.knocked about: turned round, so RES runs backwards

blocks.note: ENDURES = tolerates, whose ending RES is the residence
res. = residence, as in estate agents' listings

annotation.surface: A customer finally puts up with having their home roughed up.
annotation.walkthrough: ENDURES has RES at the end: reverse that residence and ENDURES becomes ENDUSER.
annotation.definitionFit: A business term: the final buyer of a product, after all the middlemen, is the customer in the last place.

entries.clue: Scrap line introduced by coder (6)

indicatorNotes.introduced by: preceded by, so MORSE comes first

blocks.note: Samuel Morse, who gave his name to Morse code

annotation.surface: A programmer adds a line of code and then deletes it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coder' reads as a programmer; it is Morse, the man behind Morse code.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small bite of food, or a small piece of anything, is a scrap.

entries.clue: Languishing composer, tense inside, rolling smoke (9)

indicatorNotes.inside: T goes in the composer's name
indicatorNotes.rolling: rolled over, so CIG turns round

blocks.note: Franz Lehár, composer of The Merry Widow

annotation.surface: A tense, weary composer rolls a cigarette.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rolling smoke' is someone rolling a cigarette; here rolling reverses the letters of CIG.
annotation.definitionFit: Languishing and lethargic both mean listless and without energy.

entries.clue: Following beam, losing sight of its origin (5)

indicatorNotes.losing sight of its origin: losing its origin, its first letter

blocks.note: a rafter is a roof beam

annotation.surface: Someone follows a beam of light but loses sight of its source.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beam' suggests light, which is why 'losing sight' fits; it is a roof beam, a rafter.
annotation.definitionFit: After means following, as in 'the day after'.

entries.clue: Son to cook with little butter maybe (5)

blocks.note: a butter is a goat, and a young goat is a kid
to do food is to cook it

annotation.surface: Telling one's son to cook with a small knob of butter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butter' in a kitchen scene is dairy; here it is an animal that butts, a goat.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Son' and 'kiddo' are both affectionate ways of addressing a youngster.

entries.clue: Raise cap when freed of constraints by court (5)

indicatorNotes.freed of constraints: the letters constraining it on the outside are removed

blocks.note: a beret is a cap, and without its outer letters leaves ERE

annotation.surface: Someone lifts a hat after being released by the court.
annotation.walkthrough: The courtroom surface makes 'freed of constraints' sound like a prisoner released; it strips B and T off BERET.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting up a building or a mast is lifting it upright.

entries.clue: Footballers less happy about noise when playing (9)

indicatorNotes.happy about: letters happily messing about, so they are rearranged
indicatorNotes.when playing: letters that are playing are larking about rather than standing in line, so they end up rearranged

annotation.surface: Footballers complain about crowd noise during games.
annotation.walkthrough: The Lionesses are the England women's football team.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the nickname of England's women's national football team, European champions in 2022.

entries.clue: Top holiday, though case lost twice (3)

indicatorNotes.case lost twice: the case is the outer letters, and they come off two times

blocks.note: used as printed, then stripped of its outer letters twice

annotation.surface: A great holiday, even if a suitcase went missing on both flights.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' is luggage on the surface and the outside of a word in the wordplay: strip H and Y, then O and A, to leave LID.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the cover screwed onto a jar is its top.

entries.clue: One trying education the second time leaving shocked (7)

indicatorNotes.the second time leaving: time is T, and leaving means departing, so the second T in the word departs

blocks.note: T = time; the second T in TASTER is removed

annotation.surface: Someone attempting a second go at education leaves in shock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The second time' reads as a second attempt; it picks the second T in TASTER to delete.
annotation.definitionFit: Tasered means hit with a Taser, a stun gun that gives an electric shock.

entries.clue: Ordinary bronze set back Russian runner (7)

indicatorNotes.set back: put backwards, so TAN is reversed

blocks.note: a bronze or tan is a suntan colour
the Ural is a Russian river, and rivers run

annotation.surface: A plain bronze medal set back a Russian athlete.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is an athlete on the surface and a river underneath.
annotation.definitionFit: Natural and ordinary both describe what is normal and unaffected.
